title: A turning layer says what it turns around, and you drag that point on the picture
goal: A bell that swings hangs from its mount, not from its middle. So when a layer is set to turn, the point it turns around shows up on the picture as a handle you can drag, and dragging it is what turns a wobbling blob into a swinging bell.
notes:
Slice 2 of 5 from the answered study. Depends on the motion model landing first.

MOCK: docs/design/mocks/pages/icon-animate-wt.html steps 4 and 5. Step 4 deliberately shows the WRONG thing: with the pivot at the layer centre the bell rocks like a bobblehead. Step 5 drags the pivot to the mount and it becomes a bell. That repair is the argument for the feature, so build the handle, not a hidden field.

The Around row in the Motion entry carries the named spots and the numbers; the handle carries the drag. Both write the same value.

Next release only.
acceptance: Adding a turn to a layer puts a visible pivot handle on the picture straight away, at the middle of that layer
Dragging the handle moves what the layer turns around, and the motion updates while you drag
The same point can be set by name (its centre, top centre, bottom centre) or by typing two numbers, for the times a number is what you want
Undo takes back a pivot move
The pivot is stored with the motion in PhotonzCore, tested first, and the renderer turns the layer about it
